# Returning where the course branches

<!-- Generated by build_result_registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

> What returns can be had at every step; every configuration returns exactly where each region the process stays in keeps all its possibilities. Keeping every possibility does not give returning; merging nothing gives it along runs in finitely many configurations, and a merge may lose no possibility.

`returning-where-the-course-branches` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01

Editable record: [returning-where-the-course-branches.json](returning-where-the-course-branches.json) · [Register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

<a id="主张-claim"></a>
## Claim

For a process P: a configuration can be had n steps on (Branching.Reachable) where some course of n moves leads to it; it returns (Branching.Returns) where a step from it leads to where it can be had again; a process merges (Branching.Merges, Branching.Lossless) where two distinct configurations step to one. Under a determined law each is R6's (law_reachable_iff, law_returns_iff, law_lossless_iff, law_merges_iff, law_keeps_iff). With no premise: a possibility lost stays lost (Branching.lost_stays); a configuration that returns can be had at every step (Branching.Returns.reachable), so where every configuration returns every possibility is kept (keeps_of_returns); every possibility is kept exactly where every configuration can be had at the next step (keeps_iff_fed). The exact condition for returning: a configuration returns exactly where its own course can have it at the next step (returns_iff_fed_ahead); every configuration returns exactly where every region the process never leaves keeps every possibility of its own (returns_iff_keepsWithin, returns_iff_fedWithin, keepsWithin_iff_fedWithin), with no finiteness used. Along runs, within finitely many configurations: where nothing merges every configuration of a run comes back on the run (Lossless.comes_back, Lossless.recurs), a configuration at which a run begins returns (Branching.Lossless.returns), a quantity nondecreasing along the run is constant (Branching.Lossless.no_rise), and a strict rise of such a quantity contradicts losslessness (Branching.rise_not_lossless, concluding ¬ Lossless P rather than supplying a witness of Merges), and merging nothing with a configuration that never returns needs openness (Branching.Lossless.unlisted). Witnesses: in Transit every configuration can move and every possibility is kept, yet between never returns (Transit.keeps_not_returns); OneWay merges false and true, both return, and every possibility is kept (OneWay.merge_keeps); Unfolding's Fork merges nothing and its origin never returns, its ends being unable to move, so Lossless.returns needs its run (fork_lossless_not_returns); merged stays merged needs determinacy (Determined.stays_merged; Coarse.meet_and_part). No premise.

Canonical source: [Branching.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Branching.lean)

<a id="前提与对应-hypotheses-and-correspondence"></a>
## Hypotheses and correspondence

- The laws along runs take a run as given: building a run from every configuration that can move needs choosing a continuation at each step, which is a choice.
- The laws along runs require a list holding the run's configurations (finitely many configurations).

P81 (work board), following Ren's “move towards 100%” of 12 October 2026: R6's three-way equivalence fails for laws that are not determined (with a→a, a→b, b→c, c→c, b never returns); Ren then compared this with Feynman diagrams (see P82). This states R6's laws for every process. Reading (the AI's, adopted on Ren's delegation): where the course branches, returning asks more than keeping every possibility; R6's “losing nothing is returning” is a law of determined change within finitely many configurations, and under every process it holds along each run. See the integration document §99.
